current_leader.name: Merchant settlement acceleration decision engine
current_leader.state_transition: processor balance eligible -> free payout ETA and paid speed tiers known -> external liquidity and obligations reveal actual shortfall -> choose zero/next-day/same-day/instant and minimum amount -> verify acceleration fees avoided
current_leader.why_survived: No newly tested family beat the leader. Existing evidence establishes a recurring paid-speed event with deterministic marginal cost, while exact cross-system minimum-necessary-acceleration decisioning remains unconfirmed. Leakage magnitude still lacks a merchant-level counterfactual dataset.
current_leader.strongest_evidence: Prior Adyen/Vagaro evidence establishes repeated instant-payout use; processor fee ladders make the financial delta deterministic. This run found no stronger counterfactual leakage evidence, so Gate 2 remains uncertain.
current_leader.closest_threat: First-party payout controls plus treasury/cash forecasting can absorb the wedge; fee-free faster-access products neutralize it for subsets.
current_leader.smallest_intervention: Read PSP balances/ETAs/fee tiers, bank liquidity and obligations; recommend no acceleration or cheapest sufficient speed and minimum amount; no payout execution or custody.
current_leader.monetization: Small per valuable decision, low recurring micro-fee, or capped share of verified acceleration fees avoided versus competent cash management.
current_leader.biggest_unresolved_risk: Paid acceleration may be rational liquidity demand rather than waste; avoidable volume is still unquantified.
current_leader.next_research_test: Find merchant-level/anonymized evidence linking paid accelerated payouts to external liquidity and obligations, or an exact competitor combining those inputs. Kill if avoidable fraction is immaterial or exact functionality is found.

candidate_events.fatal_flaw: Credits can expire and are machine-readable, but automatic rescue requires steering workload/request execution, overlapping the previously rejected routing family; recommendation-only value is weaker and broad credit/balance tooling already exists.
Gate 8: current commitment-intelligence and billing systems already pace commitments, forecast term-end outcomes, track rollover/expiry, and recommend plays; Drawdown is especially close.

new_search_rules: For prepaid-credit expiry, distinguish balance visibility from a monetizable rescue action; if rescue requires owning workload routing, penalize Gate 7 heavily.
Commitment tracking alone is no longer whitespace; require a narrower micro-decision not already covered by commitment-intelligence/billing suites.
Do not promote a candidate merely because forfeiture is deterministic; prove the intervention can alter the outcome without creating artificial workload or demand.
